name: NODEVOICE-LOCKED-BUILD-DEPENDENCIES-01
head: d225bcaf64008ee522bc66d40aa72eb0381b95a6
recommendation: Lock-only repair at the seven exact minimum rows. Keep package.json ranges and every unrelated row byte-identical after native resolution; no new final dependency, override, force or peer bypass.
finalOwners: later separately reviewed handoff/evidence receipt metadata
transientOwnerIfRootApproves: package.json may need temporary exact native resolver constraints for the seven existing packages; preserve and restore original bytes before final lock refresh. No install/build while temporary roots exist. This is a proposed mechanism, not one already executed.
nativeResolutionBoundary: Use native npm to generate version/resolved/integrity and row flags. Do not hand-author lock rows or transplant a context-dependent fixture. Default npm update would now choose browserslist4.28.9/postcss8.5.28 and exceed the exact minimum cohort. Stop and show the complete lock diff if native resolution adds unrelated rows or cannot return to the original root manifest.

paths: dev root postcss^8.5.16 / @tailwindcss/postcss4.3.2 / vite8.1.3 → postcss8.5.16 → nanoid3.3.15
runtimeApplicability.sourceInspection: No postcss/browserslist/nanoid match in application src, Convex or scripts; configured PostCSS build plugins are Tailwind and Autoprefixer. Installed postcss/lib/input.js calls nanoid/non-secure with fixed6.
runtimeApplicability.productionAudit: NOT_RUN in this recon; lock marks all three dev:true. No claim of zero production vulnerability audit.

regressionPlan: Preserve reviewed2UIowners, original package/lock,177source,3dist,refs/index and installed baseline before any mutation; wait for source/publication review closure.

Resolve the exact seven-node minimum cohort natively in the existing candidate only after approval, restore original package.json bytes, inspect all lock rows and verify registry integrity/constraints. Keep update-browserslist-db1.2.3,picocolors1.1.1,source-map-js1.2.1 unchanged.
Run one normal npm ci from final lock, then full npm audit and npm audit --omit=dev; retain raw outcomes and distinguish metadata/feed state from applicability.

Run bounded old/new canaries in owned scratch processes: negative/zero nanoid generator with a short child deadline; harmless local PostCSS source-map marker with from set/unset and literal read observer; Browserslist inherited-key stats and varied-query sustained scenario without forcing an OOM. Old failure must be observed and safe generated fixtures retained.
Run ordinary npm run doctor, npm run proof (55 tests/9 files plus CLI), npm run build with deterministic/no-key environment and full source guards.

Compare rebuilt served JS/CSS/HTML and a small native current320/390/1440 controls/room check. If CSS or output differs, bind affected before/after geometry/pixels. Do not claim new final100 playback from an older build: unchanged relevant output may be explicitly rebound; changed runtime output requires the named current-tree100 proof or an honest historical hold.
Freeze exact source/lock/installed/build/canary/audit evidence for nonauthor review; no push, deployment, timeout or provider change.
limits: Reconnaissance only: no npm install/update/audit fix, lock/source edit, package execution, provider call or environment-value retrieval.
The seven target versions are the smallest verified metadata combination clearing the six recorded advisory ranges; they are not an executed npm resolution or a current whole-graph audit result.

No externally supplied CSS/stats/query/size path was found in src/convex/scripts. This is bounded source inspection, not a complete exploitability proof. Build/PR tooling remains relevant even for dev dependencies.

npm start uses tsx, itself a devDependency; an npm ci --omit=dev deployment is not certified. The three affected libraries are outside the inspected application request path, not necessarily absent from an installed production host.
The npm feed labels the Browserslist cache issue high; its maintainer advisory says moderate. Preserve both source classifications without changing the baseline three-high package count.
GHSA-xwg4-73v4-xw9w is already fixed in nanoid3.3.12; current3.3.15 is outside that range. Do not add it as a current fourth finding.
One supporting registry request batch using the abbreviated metadata Accept header failed406; the corrected application/json reads all passed. No candidate state changed.
